title: Kernels, /boot, Live Patching, and Planned Reboots
intro: Kernel updates are the patches that need reboots, and reboots are where fleets get hurt. Know which kernel is running, keep /boot from filling up, use live patching to buy time, and reboot deliberately.

steps.prompt: Show the kernel that's actually running.
steps.why: The installed kernel and the running kernel differ until a reboot. Vulnerability scanners that check installed packages will call the host patched while it's still running the vulnerable kernel. Always check uname -r.

steps.prompt: List installed kernel packages on this Ubuntu host.
steps.fake_output:
ii  linux-image-5.15.0-105-generic  5.15.0-105.115  amd64
ii  linux-image-5.15.0-112-generic  5.15.0-112.122  amd64
ii  linux-image-5.15.0-119-generic  5.15.0-119.129  amd64
ii  linux-image-5.15.0-122-generic  5.15.0-122.132  amd64
ii  linux-image-generic             5.15.0.122.122  amd64
steps.explanation: Four kernels installed; 122 is newest, 119 is running.
steps.why: Old kernels pile up in /boot, which is often a small separate partition. When it fills, the next kernel update fails halfway (servers-incident-004).

steps.fake_output:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda2       488M  401M   51M  89% /boot
steps.explanation: 89% full: one more kernel won't fit.
steps.why: Each kernel and its initramfs take roughly 80-120MB. Monitor /boot like any other filesystem; it's often left out of disk alerts.

steps.prompt: Remove kernels (and other packages) that are no longer needed.
steps.fake_output:
The following packages will be REMOVED:
  linux-image-5.15.0-105-generic* linux-modules-5.15.0-105-generic*
  linux-image-5.15.0-112-generic* linux-modules-5.15.0-112-generic*
0 upgraded, 0 newly installed, 4 to remove and 0 not upgraded.
After this operation, 412 MB disk space will be freed.
steps.explanation: Old kernels removed; the running (119) and newest (122) stay.
steps.why: apt protects the running kernel and the newest one, so autoremove is safe here. Never remove the running kernel by hand. On RHEL, 'installonly_limit' in dnf.conf caps how many kernels are kept automatically.

steps.prompt: This host is enrolled in Canonical Livepatch. Check whether the critical kernel fix is already applied live, without a reboot.
steps.fake_output:
last check: 12 minutes ago
kernel: 5.15.0-119.129-generic
server check-in: succeeded
patch state: ✓ all applicable livepatch modules inserted
patch version: 112.1
tier: updates (Free usage)
fixes:
  * CVE-2024-36971 (high)
steps.explanation: The high-severity CVE is patched in the running kernel.
steps.why: Live patching (Canonical Livepatch, RHEL kpatch) fixes critical kernel CVEs in memory. It buys time to schedule reboots properly; it doesn't replace them, because not every fix can be live-patched.

steps.prompt: Schedule this host's reboot in 5 minutes with a message to logged-in users.
steps.fake_output:
Reboot scheduled for Sun 2026-09-28 10:47:00 UTC, use 'shutdown -c' to cancel.
Broadcast message from root@web-02: Rebooting for kernel update
steps.explanation: A reboot in 5 minutes; logged-in users are warned.
steps.why: A delayed reboot gives people a chance to save work and gives you a chance to cancel ('shutdown -c'). For a fleet, reboots belong in a rolling playbook: drain, reboot, verify, re-add (servers-tutorial-003).
